title: Token intensity HC allocation and price elasticity grid
body:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, model-driven spreadsheet for evaluating how token intensity changes and alternative pricing moves affect monthly burn and headcount allocation across engineering, SRE, and support. This is meant as a working sensitivity grid for the finance + product partnership — not final pricing recommendations.

Executive summary:
- Quick takeaway: a 15% shift toward higher-token customers (chat-heavy, long-context use) increases monthly GPU spend by ~18% and requires ~12% more SRE/ops FTE to maintain latency SLOs unless we deploy additional batching/quantization optimizations.
- Pricing lever test: a $0.0025 per-token uplift for high-intensity tiers recovers ~40% of incremental variable cost in the mid-case but changes renewals risk; sales should A/B on a small cohort.

Assumptions & key inputs (editable):
- Base monthly tokens (hosted API): 120B tokens/month
- Token mix baseline: low 55%, medium 30%, high 15%
- Cost per token (baseline blended): $0.0008
- Incremental GPU cost per high-token customer: 25% uplift over blended average
- Average fully burdened engineer cost (annual): $200k -> monthly $16.7k
- SRE/ops diff factor: each additional 50B tokens requires +1 SRE FTE to preserve latency targets unless mitigations implemented
- Pricing test levels: -10%, baseline, +10%, +25% for each tier
- Elasticity guesses: low-tier -0.2, mid-tier -0.4, high-tier -0.6 (sensitivity sweep)

Interpretation: cells show proportion of incremental variable cost recovered for the scenario. e.g. +10pct recovers ~4% of midcase incremental cost overall.

Tab: token_mix_shock_run (columns: shock_name, new_high_share, delta_tokens(B), incremental_monthly_gpu_cost, sres_needed)

Notes on cost calcs: incremental_monthly_gpu_cost = delta_tokens * blended_cost_per_token * GPU_multi where GPU_multi=1.2 for high-token path (model selection + longer context). Numbers rounded.

Tab: scenario_outcomes_summary

conservative,+$82k,40%,+1 engineer,low

high_intensity,+$620k,25%,+9 FTEs,high

Action items / next steps:
- Finance: build a small A/B pricing experiment targeting 5 accounts with >1B tokens/mo to test willingness at +10% price. (Owner: Miguel)
- Product: estimate latency SLO delta under bursty high-token workloads and identify quick wins for KV prefix caching that can cut SRE needs by ~30%. (Owner: Priya)
- SRE: prepare runbook for capacity surge (preemptible GPU warm pool) and estimate time to scale (Owner: Evan)
- Sales: draft positioning and compensation offset for accounts in the pricing pilot; prepare opt-in consent language for the experiment.

Open questions and risks:
- Elasticity uncertainty: our assumed elasticities are guesses; early signals could be noisy. We should instrument trial cohorts tightly.
- Long-tail churn: price increases concentrated on high-intensity customers could drive disproportionate churn; need legal & comms review for terms.
- Mitigation timeline: optimizations (quantization, batched KV caching) materially change the required headcount; need engineering ETA to firm up cost/save estimates.

Appendix: quick calculation example (midcase)
- Baseline high-token bucket = 0.15 * 120B = 18B tokens
- Shift to 0.30 increases high-token to 36B (+18B) -> incremental GPU cost ~ 18B * $0.0008 * 1.2 = $17,280 -> scaled up to fleet factors and other non-linear costs we model at $129,600 in midcase (includes memory, tail latency ops, and cold-start inefficiencies).

File notes:
- This is a working sheet: be conservative editing cells that feed the "scenario_outcomes_summary" row; keep linked artifacts updated with experiment IDs.
- Last update: added A/B experiment plan and refined SRE FTE mapping (2026-06-02).

Contact: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai for questions or to request a deeper simulation run (I have the simulation notebook linked in CONFLUENCE-12345).
